ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a spherical Earth, with the vertical dashed line being the rotation axis, and the top end of the axis marked with angular velocity ω. The equatorial plane passes through center O, and point C is located on the equator; point A is north of the equator and is marked with 30° related to the equator; point B is south of the equator and is marked with 60°. Reasoning: When a point on the Earth's surface rotates with the Earth, both its linear velocity and centripetal acceleration depend on the distance from that point to the rotation axis. The distance from a point at latitude φ to the rotation axis is the radius of the latitude circle r = R cos φ. Point A has latitude 30°N, so r_A = R cos 30° = (√3/2)R. Point B has latitude 60°S; take the magnitude of the latitude as 60°, so r_B = R cos 60° = (1/2)R. The magnitude of the centripetal acceleration a_c = ω²r, therefore a_A:a_B = r_A:r_B = √3:1.

raw_record.question_text:
Points A, B, and C are located on the Earth's surface at latitudes of 30° North, 60° South, and the equator, respectively. The Earth's radius is given as $R$, and its angular velocity of rotation is $\omega$.

1. Determine the ratio of the magnitudes of the linear velocities of points A and B.
2. Determine the ratio of the magnitudes of the centripetal accelerations of points A and B.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows a spherical Earth rotating about a vertical axis with angular velocity ω; the equator is drawn through point C, point A is marked at 30° north of the equator, and point B is marked at 60° south. Use the text to take Earth radius as R and the requested comparison as A versus B. For a point at latitude φ, its distance from the rotation axis is the radius of its latitude circle, r = R cos φ. Thus r_A = R cos 30° = (√3/2)R and r_B = R cos 60° = (1/2)R. Since all surface points share the same angular velocity ω, linear speed is v = ωr, so v_A:v_B = r_A:r_B = √3:1. Centripetal acceleration toward the rotation axis is a_c = ω²r, so a_A:a_B = r_A:r_B = √3:1.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the vertical line is the Earth's rotation axis, the curved horizontal circle represents the equator, and A and B lie on different latitude circles, with A closer to the equator than B. Read from the text that A is at 30° N and B is at 60° S, and that both rotate with the same angular velocity ω. Instead of starting from v = ωr directly, compare the actual circular paths completed in one rotation period T = 2π/ω. The circumference traveled by a latitude point is 2πR cos φ. Therefore A travels 2πR cos 30° per period and B travels 2πR cos 60° per period, so v_A/v_B = [2πR cos 30°/T]/[2πR cos 60°/T] = √3. For acceleration, use a_c = v²/r for circular motion, where r is the latitude-circle radius. Since v = circumference/T is proportional to r for the same T, a_c = v²/r is also proportional to r; hence a_A/a_B = r_A/r_B = cos 30°/cos 60° = √3:1.

推理：题目给出 A 在北纬 30°，B 在南纬 60°，地球自转角速度相同，均为 ω。按指定方法，不直接从 v=ωr 开始，而比较同一自转周期 T=2π/ω 内两点走过的纬度圈周长。纬度为 φ 的点到自转轴的距离，即纬度圈半径，为 R cos φ，所以一周走过的路程为 2πR cos φ。A 点每周期走过 2πR cos30°，B 点每周期走过 2πR cos60°。因此 v_A/v_B = (2πR cos30°/T)/(2πR cos60°/T) = cos30°/cos60° = (√3/2)/(1/2) = √3。对于向心加速度，用 a_c = v²/r，其中 r 是纬度圈半径。由于两点周期相同，v 与 r 成正比，所以 a_c = v²/r 也与 r 成正比。因此 a_A/a_B = r_A/r_B = cos30°/cos60° = √3。
